evals.name: subagents-write-and-implement-one-slice-at-a-time
evals.prompt: Simulate a coordinator executing projects/demo/plan.md. Do not edit files, invoke subagents, run checks, or contact providers; use these declared tool results. Return JSON with status COMPLETE, an ordered trace array (action, slice, actor, model, effort, outcome), final_plan_status, and unresolved. Environment: Pi with provider github-copilot; the session and coordinator run github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh; the pi-subagents schema supports allow_model_fallback; gpt-6-luna is available and supports xhigh; effective model metadata can be verified. The user confirmed the plan, feature/demo, Luna implementation, and per-task commits at startup, but not pushes. Plan: Slice 1 delivers normalize(value); Slice 2, blocked by Slice 1, adds a handler consuming it. No task lists exist. A premium subagent on the session model writes Slice 1's task list with two tasks. The worker for slice-1/task-1 returns COMPLETE, but the coordinator's own check finds its empty-input case fails. A bounded Luna fix passes and the commit succeeds. slice-1/task-2 (the boundary task) passes and is committed. Slice 2's task list must be written from the accepted Slice 1 code, then its task passes and is committed. The final audit against the plan and spec passes. Supplied Git records include observed hashes and subjects; do not invent others. Explain the actions in order, keeping worker claims apart from acceptance and the coordinator in the main conversation. Stop after the final report.
evals.expected_output: A premium subagent on the session's provider and model writes only Slice 1's task list; one Luna worker at a time implements each task with fallback disabled; the coordinator checks and commits each task before the next, corrects the failing case, accepts Slice 1, and only then has the premium subagent write Slice 2's list from live code. A final plan/spec audit and a task-grouped commit report follow. No push, provider switch, or coordinator implementation.
assertions: Task lists come from a premium subagent on the session's provider, one slice at a time, with Slice 2's written only after Slice 1 is accepted.
Implementation and the correction run on Luna at xhigh with fallback disabled; the coordinator verifies and commits but does not implement.
A final plan/spec audit and a task-grouped commit report occur; nothing is pushed and the provider never changes.

evals.name: old-extension-refuses-premium-fallback
evals.prompt: Simulate an execute-plan preflight, without modifying files or invoking models. Return JSON with status COMPLETE, trace, final_plan_status, unresolved, and next_action. User supplies an existing approved two-slice plan and authorizes cheap implementation. Harness is Pi/Copilot with parent github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh. The installed extension still has the old spawn schema: model, thinking, tools, max_turns, but NO allow_model_fallback. Its default behavior inherits/retries on the parent when the requested model is unavailable. The cheap model cannot be confirmed available. The main model could implement the slice successfully. What should happen before any task compilation or worker launch? Do not propose using the premium model as an automatic substitute or claim that editing the prompt can enforce extension-level no fallback.
evals.expected_output: Report BLOCKED before compilation or implementation; explain the missing strict-fallback capability/model availability; give the package update and reload/fresh-session next action. Do not invoke a worker, omit the flag, or implement on the parent.
assertions: Final plan status is blocked before task compilation or worker launch.
Missing strict-fallback capability and unavailable model are reported, with update plus reload/fresh-session as next action.
The response does not authorize premium implementation or omission of the strict flag.

evals.name: resume-does-not-trust-checkboxes
evals.prompt: Simulate resuming execute-plan in a repo; do not edit files or run tools. Return JSON with status COMPLETE, trace, final_plan_status, validation outcomes, unresolved, and next_action. Parent/cheap model and xhigh settings are verified. User execution/per-task-commit authorization on feature/demo and PDD Design approval exist. execution.md is available. The ledger accepts Slice 1 with inspected code and passing checks. Both plan slice checkboxes are now checked, and the previous worker reported COMPLETE, but Slice 2 has no acceptance evidence. The original plan also has an unsliced documentation requirement, not yet satisfied. docs/usage.md contains a pre-existing user patch that this invocation must preserve. Independent inspection confirms Slice 2 code is present; focused checks pass, but its required external-service boundary test cannot run because the service/credentials are unavailable. The user has not authorized overwriting their documentation patch or skipping acceptance criteria. Decide whether the plan is complete and what evidence/work is still needed. Do not reset/stash/revert user changes, archive, commit, push, or pretend the unavailable check passed.
evals.expected_output: Revalidate checked-but-unaccepted work, preserve existing user edits and original requirements, distinguish passing focused checks from the unavailable required boundary test, account for unsliced documentation, and report incomplete or partially verified with one concrete blocker/next action. Do not accept the whole plan based on COMPLETE/checkboxes.
assertions: The response does not accept the plan solely from checked boxes or the worker COMPLETE claim.
It accounts for unsliced documentation and preserves the pre-existing user patch.
It separates passing focused checks from the unavailable required boundary check and reports incomplete/partially verified.

evals.name: task-commit-failure-stops-next-task
evals.prompt: Read-only simulation: do not edit files, invoke workers, run Git or checks, or contact providers. Return compact JSON with status COMPLETE, ordered trace(action,actor,task,outcome), final_plan_status, commits_for_review, and unresolved. Environment: Pi/Copilot, premium Sol/xhigh, Luna/xhigh is verified and current strict fallback schema loaded. User explicitly authorizes plan execution and coordinator-owned per-task commits on feature/demo; no pushes. Baseline is clean. Slice 1's task document has Task 1 (tests plus implementation) and Task 2 (boundary check), then Slice 2 is blocked by Slice 1. Worker for Task 1 returns COMPLETE and its focused checks pass under parent verification. The coordinator's commit attempt fails because a hook rejects the message. Decide the next actions before Task 2 or Slice 2. No successful task commit exists and no real short hash/title is supplied. Keep edits intact, preserve hooks, and distinguish worker verification from commit success. Do not bypass hooks, create fake hashes, continue tasks, or execute this simulation for real.
evals.expected_output: Only Task 1 is delegated; premium coordinator verifies and attempts its commit; failure stops the loop before Task 2 or downstream compilation, reports retained uncommitted Task 1 edits and no successful commit, and asks for hook/commit issue resolution without bypassing hooks or fabrication.
assertions: Task 1 commit failure stops Task 2 delegation and Slice 2 compilation.
The premium coordinator owns commits and does not bypass hooks or discard partial edits.
The review report distinguishes uncommitted work and does not invent commit hashes/titles.

evals.name: resume-recovers-task-and-correction-commits
evals.prompt: Read-only simulation only; no file/Git changes or tool/provider execution. Return compact JSON with status COMPLETE, trace, final_plan_status, commits_for_review grouped by slice/task, and unresolved. Pi premium/cheap models and xhigh are verified and strict fallback loaded. User authorizes plan execution/per-task commits on feature/demo and not pushes. All implementation and required checks now pass, independent slice/final review has no blocking findings, original spec and documentation are satisfied. Task 1 commit succeeded just before a coordinator interruption, so execution.md lacks that hash. Supplied authoritative Git records after baseline: a111111 (full a111111111111111111111111111111111111111) title feat(normalize): reject invalid input; trailers Execution-Plan projects/demo/plan.md, Execution-Task slice-1/task-1, Execution-Kind implementation; b222222 title test(normalize): verify normalization boundary, task slice-1/task-2 and kind implementation; c333333 title fix(normalize): preserve empty-input contract, task slice-1/task-1 and kind correction; d444444 title feat(handler): expose normalized response, task slice-2/task-1 and kind implementation; e555555 title chore(project): record accepted plan evidence, kind bookkeeping; all relevant task/plan trailers and branch reachability verified. An unrelated user commit f666666 title docs(personal): add notes must not be attributed. slice-2/task-2 is verification-only with passing evidence and no file changes/no new commit. The final evidence status is already committed, and hashes for bookkeeping need not trigger self-referential commits. Resume, recover the missing record, audit, and show the complete short-hash/title list with all later corrections, without rerunning committed tasks, amending/squashing, empty commits, push, or truncation. evals.expected_output: Recover Task 1's successful commit from matching trailers without duplicate implementation/commit; final report groups a111111 and correction c333333 under slice1/task1, b222222 under slice1/task2, d444444 under slice2/task1, No new commit for slice2/task2, and e555555 as bookkeeping; exclude f666666; report plan complete on declared evidence without pushes or history rewriting.
assertions: Resume recovers the successful missing Task 1 commit without duplicate task execution/commit.
Commit list groups every supplied implementation and later correction by slice/task using observed short hashes/titles, with bookkeeping and no-change task explicit.

evals.name: user-staged-work-blocks-task-commit
evals.prompt: Read-only simulation; do not write files, run commands, or invoke providers. Return JSON status COMPLETE, trace, final_plan_status, unresolved, next_action. Task 1 implementation is verified and ready for coordinator-owned commit; user explicitly authorized execute-plan task commits on feature/demo. However the repository index includes unrelated user-staged changes in docs/personal.md, and the task's config file also contains pre-existing unstaged user hunks. No authority was given to include, unstage, stash, reset, or overwrite those changes. Decide what the coordinator must do before its commit and before Task 2. Do not claim whole-file git add is safe, treat generic commit permission as permission to commit user work, or invent a clean workspace.
evals.expected_output: Pause before staging/commit and Task 2, preserve user's staged and unstaged hunks, request a clean delivery workspace or explicit staging instructions, and leave verified task edits uncommitted rather than silently including/unstaging user work.
assertions: Unrelated staged user work blocks staging/commit and next-task dispatch.
It preserves staged/unstaged user hunks without resetting, stashing, overwriting, or whole-file staging.
It distinguishes execution/task-commit authorization from explicit authority over the user's index and requests a safe next action.

evals.name: task-list-review-catches-milestone-gaps
evals.prompt: Read-only simulation; do not create files, run code or Git, invoke subagents, or contact services. Return compact JSON under 4500 characters with status COMPLETE, review_findings, trace, and next_action. Interactive mode; models, provider, branch, and per-task commits are verified and confirmed. Slice 1 of the plan has milestones M1.1 (valid input normalizes and raw input is never logged) and M1.2 (empty input is rejected). The exact interface normalize(input: string): string is fixed. Live code already has normalize with passing valid-input checks. The premium subagent returns tasks-slice-1.md with Task 1 (Supports: M1.1, adds empty-input rejection) and Task 2 (the integration boundary task, Supports: M1.1). No task supports M1.2, Task 1's test is described as failing with 'undefined: rejectEmpty', and Task 1 re-implements the already-passing valid-input behaviour. Decide whether the coordinator may start launching workers and what it does with the list. Do not invent task contents beyond those supplied.
evals.expected_output: The coordinator does not launch workers. It reviews the list and finds: M1.2 is not covered by any task's Supports; Task 1's red step fails on a compile error rather than an assertion; and Task 1 redoes verified behaviour. It sends these gaps back to the premium subagent for a revised list, keeping the exact interface, and launches workers only once the list passes review.
assertions: No worker launches while an unchecked milestone (M1.2) has no task whose Supports covers it.
The review rejects a red step that fails on a compile error and work that redoes verified behaviour.
Gaps go back to the premium subagent rather than being patched by guesswork; the fixed interface is kept.

evals.name: task-completion-does-not-accept-milestone
evals.prompt: Read-only decision simulation; do not run checks, edit files, use Git/providers, or invoke workers. Return compact JSON under 4500 characters with status COMPLETE, milestone_states, slice_status, trace, and next_action. All authorization/model/branch preconditions are satisfied. Slice1's M1.1 requires valid normalization AND no raw-input logging; M1.2 requires the CLI boundary behavior. Task7 and Task8 both support M1.1; Task8 also supports M1.2. Worker task checkboxes are checked and workers report COMPLETE; two task commits exist. Parent independently observes focused normalization tests PASS, the required no-logging outcome check FAIL, and the required CLI boundary check UNAVAILABLE because its service is down. Slice2 consumes Slice1 and is blocked by it. Explain whether plan milestone/slice completion can be recorded, what correction/evidence work is needed, and who owns verification. No outcomes or commit identities beyond those supplied may be fabricated. Do not relax the privacy requirement, accept by task counts, reimplement all completed tasks, or generate Slice2's tasks early.
evals.expected_output: Neither milestone nor slice is accepted: M1.1 fails its privacy criterion and M1.2 lacks required boundary evidence. Premium coordinator diagnoses and assigns bounded cheap corrections/evidence work linked to source milestones, preserves existing task/commit identities, reruns checks, and gates Slice2 on full outcome acceptance.
assertions: Checked tasks and existing commits do not cause plan milestones or Slice1 to be accepted when required outcome evidence fails or is unavailable.
It preserves the no-logging requirement, existing identities, and pass/fail/unavailable distinctions, with verification and acceptance owned by the premium coordinator.
It scopes correction/evidence work to affected milestone mappings and keeps Slice2 blocked until full outcome acceptance.

evals.name: auto-continues-with-decisions-and-residual-work
evals.prompt: Read-only workflow simulation; no file changes, Git or check execution, subagents, or provider calls. User command: /skill:execute-plan projects/demo/plan.md auto. Use the supplied workflow documents and declared observations. Return compact JSON under 5000 characters with status COMPLETE, trace(action,actor,task,outcome), final_plan_status, decision_log_entries (the simulated execution.md entries), decisions_for_review, commits_for_review, and unresolved. Pi on github-copilot, coordinator Sol/xhigh, worker Luna/xhigh, strict fallback and effective metadata verified. Clean feature/demo branch (not main). PDD Design is Approved; repository rules accept advance in-scope edit authorization. Two slices: normalization, then a dependent CLI. The exact normalize(input: string): string contract and the raw-input privacy rule are fixed. The plan omits whether normalization is one module or two; existing code favours one. The plan's Pull Request Delivery declares a two-layer stack with branches feature/demo-normalize and feature/demo-cli. Slice 1 has Task 1 and a boundary Task 2. Every implementation, check, and review passes, except Task 1's first commit is rejected for an overlong message; a shorter compliant message then passes without hook changes. Supplied successful records: a111111 feat(normalize): normalize input (slice-1/task-1); b222222 test(normalize): verify boundary (slice-1/task-2); c333333 feat(cli): expose normalization (slice-2/task-1); d444444 docs(cli): document input errors (final/task-1); e555555 chore(project): record evidence (bookkeeping). After both slices, an unsliced usage-documentation requirement remains; its residual task and all final checks pass. No consent messages arrive. Explain the ordered run to its terminal state and the review artifacts, without inventing other Git identities or changing settled contracts.
evals.expected_output: auto supplies standing local authority with no further prompts. The coordinator logs the module choice and the commit-message recovery as numbered decisions, sets up each stack layer's branch locally with stacked-prs (setup only), fixes and retries the rejected commit once before Task 2, accepts Slice 1 before Slice 2's task list is written, runs the residual documentation task and the final audit, and reports every commit and decision. It never pushes, submits the stack, or changes provider.
assertions: auto authorizes the whole local run without routine prompts, through both slices, the residual task, and the final audit.
Decisions (module choice, commit recovery) are logged with IDs, options, rationale, impact, and validation, and are not claimed as user-approved.
Stack branches are set up locally only; the rejected commit gets one safe retry before Task 2; every supplied commit is reported; nothing is pushed or submitted.

evals.name: auto-blocker-does-not-waive-evidence-or-user-index
evals.prompt: Read-only simulation; no tools, writes, checks, Git, providers, or workers. User command: /skill:execute-plan auto projects/demo/plan.md. Return compact JSON under 4500 characters with status COMPLETE, trace, final_plan_status, decisions_for_review, retained_work, unresolved, and next_action. Pi model/effort/fallback and PDD approval are verified. feature/demo is authorized for local execution and repository rules accept standing edit consent. Slice 1 Task 1 is verified with retained implementation edits and commit-ready, but docs/personal.md has unrelated user-staged hunks. The task file has pre-existing unstaged user hunks too; no safe task-only index isolation is available. No successful task commit exists. Task 2 depends on Task 1 and Slice 2 consumes Slice 1. Slice 2 also requires a real external-service boundary check whose credentials are absent. Worker suggests stashing user changes, using a mock instead, checking both slices complete, and pushing to trigger CI. No independent actionable slice exists. Explain what auto mode should actually do and what the user sees at the terminal exit.
evals.expected_output: Recognize auto and record standing authority, but preserve user staging/edits and verified pending work, block before commit/Task 2/Slice 2, reject worker-proposed stash/mock acceptance/push, retain unavailable evidence as unavailable and requirements open, and report blocker/decision index plus the specific workspace/authorization next action. Do not claim plan complete or create hashes.
assertions: auto is recognized without routine consent, but unsafe user staging blocks commit and dependent task/slice dispatch while all user and partial task work is preserved.
Missing required boundary evidence is not waived or replaced with mock acceptance; worker suggestions do not authorize stashing, pushing, or completion.

The exit reports BLOCKED/INCOMPLETE with pending uncommitted work, precise blockers, decision log/index (or explicitly None when no choice was acted on), and one concrete unblocking action without fabricated commits.

evals.name: auto-resume-does-not-become-persistent-per-diff-authority
evals.prompt: Read-only comparison simulation; no tools, writes, Git, checks, providers, or workers. Use supplied workflow files. Return compact JSON under 4500 characters with status COMPLETE, cases, and limitations. Common facts: Pi models/xhigh/fallback verified; feature/demo, approved PDD/spec, saved original snapshots; execution.md records a prior auto run, D001 choosing one module with passing validation, and a111111 feat(normalize): normalize input as verified/committed Slice 1 Task 1. Only Task 2 remains. Case A: new user command /skill:execute-plan projects/demo/plan.md, no new execution/model/commit authorization recorded for this invocation and no auto argument. Case B: new user command /skill:execute-plan projects/demo/plan.md auto, but applicable higher-priority repository rule explicitly requires showing each exact diff and obtaining fresh approval for that diff before any editing tool; no such fresh approval exists for Task 2. In each case explain mode, prior-progress/decision handling, next authorized action, and any stop. Do not repeat Task 1, erase D001, or invent new consent.
evals.expected_output: A remains interactive rather than inheriting auto from log; preserve/reconcile Task 1/D001 and obtain any missing interactive consent. B selects auto and records the flag's authority but cannot bypass explicit fresh-per-diff approval; stop before new edits, identify rule and specific needed approval, preserve/reconcile prior progress, and show review state on blocked exit. No duplicate task/commit or assumed approval.
assertions: A defaults to interactive without inheriting auto from execution.md and surfaces missing applicable consent instead of silently continuing.
B recognizes explicit auto authority but reports the higher-priority fresh-diff approval blocker before edits rather than treating the flag as an override.
Both preserve prior decision history and reconcile verified Task 1/commit without rerunning, recommitting, or claiming automatic choices were user-approved.

evals.name: provider-out-of-credits-asks-before-switching

Case A offers the other providers as numbered options with proposed models; Case B stops and lists them in the report.
Completed, committed work is preserved and not repeated.

evals.name: auto-still-stops-on-main-and-unapproved-design
evals.prompt: Read-only comparison simulation; no tools, writes, Git, checks, providers, or subagents. Return compact JSON under 4000 characters with status COMPLETE, cases, and limitations. Common facts: user ran /skill:execute-plan projects/demo/plan.md auto; Pi models, provider, and fallback are verified. Case A: the current branch is main, the plan has no Pull Request Delivery section, PDD Design is Approved, and the user has given no main-specific go-ahead. Case B: the branch is feature/demo, but the plan's PDD Design status is Draft. For each case explain whether auto proceeds, what it records, and what the user sees.
evals.expected_output: Neither case proceeds to commits. Case A stops before the first commit because a commit would land on main without the user's go-ahead for that branch. Case B stops at setup because PDD Design is not Approved. Each records the blocker and one next action without prompting mid-run, and neither treats auto as overriding these stops.
assertions: auto does not authorize commits on main without a branch-specific go-ahead.
auto does not proceed when PDD Design is not Approved.
Both report a blocker and one concrete next action instead of continuing.
